relevance_note: Case report of an in-scope person with SSADH deficiency and an ALDH5A1 variant: "Here, we report a female infant with global developmental delay and central hypothyroidism (CH)who was diagnosed with SSADH deficiency".
method_note: Single case report. I read the whole Markdown by hand and no script transcribed any text, so every span below was copied from the text I read. The paper prints non-breaking spaces after numerals; spans keep them (written as \u00a0) so that they match the file byte for byte. In-scope people: the patient plus her two first-degree-consanguineous parents, whom the paper describes as tested carriers ("Both parents were heterozygous carriers for this variant."), giving three individuals. Tables 1 and 2 are laboratory tables for the single patient (their columns are time points, not people) and contain no cells with ' / ', so no stacked-cell (D-31) issue arose. Points I was unsure how to record: (1) age at SSADH diagnosis is never stated; the '7 months old' statements concern the admission and the tertiary hypothyroidism diagnosis, so age_at_diagnosis is 'not reported'. (2) Inheritance for the patient is recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because the paper states that both parents carry the variant and the enum has no 'both parents' option; I did not choose 'inherited maternal' or 'inherited paternal'. (3) variant_type 'missense' for the patient rests on the authors' prose "the substitution of Leu70 by a smaller and conformationally restricted proline", not on the word 'missense'. (4) Per D-29, variant type, pathogenicity, ACMG criteria and functional evidence are 'not reported' for the parents, because the paper gives those values only for the patient's variant. (5) 'intellectual disability' is left 'not reported' although the paper reports global developmental delay, which is a different concept. (6) 'exertional dyskinesia' and 'hemiballismus' are marked excluded only by subsumption under the paper's explicit "she does not have seizure disorders, dystonia, or movement disorders"; ataxia is left 'not reported'. (7) Normal findings were recorded as excluded features naming the ruled-out abnormality (D-27); for whole examinations ('Her eye examination was normal', 'an unremarkable systemic examination') I wrote 'abnormal eye examination' and 'abnormal systemic examination', which name no specific abnormality. (8) Boolean fields whose value is false (is_proband for the parents, cites_prior_report_of_same_patients) have span null, because no quote can support a negative. Inconsistencies found in the paper: the variant is classified as "a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) (class 3)" while the Discussion repeatedly argues "in favor of the variant's pathogenicity"; the Figure 5 legend gives "PDB accession 2W8R" whereas the text gives "PDB accession nr 2W8O"; Table 1 gives urine GHB 50 mg/L on levothyroxine and 25 mg/L off it, while the text says GABA/GHB levels "were reduced after two months of thyroid hormone supplementation". No previously published person is described with individual-level detail (Attri et al. and the other references are cited only at group level), so no literature-derived rows were created and those group figures were not used as evidence about the patient.

Whole‐exome sequencing revealed a previously unreported homozygous variant in the ALDH5A1 gene, NM_170740: c.209T > C; p. (Leu70Pro).

Although we have not been able to perform in vitro studies (eg, variant overexpression and wild type rescue) to confirm the pathogenicity of these variants, the presence of the biochemical phenotype demonstrated by high urinary and brain concentrations for GHB and GABA, respectively, is a convincing argument in favor of the variant's pathogenicity.

span: We describe an infant with SSADH deficiency and a unique clinical presentation of severe early onset global developmental delay, failure to thrive and evidence of a tertiary form of hypothyroidism

Her developmental assessment showed an inability to sit with support, head lag, she could not turn from the supine to prone position, and she could not hold objects, but she could follow objects with both eyes.
Currently, she is 3 years old and is able to walk and sit without support and says a few words but no sentences.
